articleTitle: Hafnia-based Ferroelectric Memory: Device Physics Strongly Correlated with Materials Chemistry
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on IC Design and Technology (ICICDT)
abstract: Ferroelectric memory devices have emerged as a promising option for the next generation of semiconductor devices, catering to both conventional and future computing paradigms. Particularly noteworthy is the disruptive acceleration of physical scaling and performance enhancement in ferroelectric memory devices, brought about by the discovery of ferroelectricity in fluorite-structured ferroelectrics like HfO2 and ZrO2. The addition of small amounts of dopants to the conventional gate insulator of metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors, followed by crystallization annealing, introduces intriguing new functionality that has captivated both academia and industry. The fluorite-structured ferroelectrics offer ample memory window in ferroelectric field-effect transistors, even at sub-10-nm thickness, owing to their impressively high coercive field of ~1.0 MV/cm. Moreover, their bandgap, exceeding 5 eV, enables effective scaling down with minimal leakage current. Additionally, their growth via atomic layer deposition ensures precise control over thickness, even on complex three-dimensional nanostructures. Nevertheless, certain challenges persist, demanding urgent solutions, such as limited endurance, device-to-device variation, and the need to strike a balance between operational speed and endurance. These issues are closely tied to the material properties and fabrication processes. Hence, this presentation offers a comprehensive review of the current challenges associated with HfO2-based ferroelectric memory devices and explores potential solutions from the perspective of materials science and engineering.

articleTitle: Energy-Efficient SRAM with Emerging Technologies
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on IC Design and Technology (ICICDT)
abstract: As data-centric applications increasingly demand high energy efficiency, there is a growing need for embedded SRAM arrays with high capacity and low operating voltages. To enhance computing capabilities, these applications require large memory capacities and compact cell areas. As computing cores continuously access on-chip SRAM caches, optimizing the density, performance, and energy efficiency of SRAM caches becomes crucial for future high-performance computing. This presentation focuses on recent studies exploring emerging technologies for SRAM, with a specific emphasis on CFET-based SRAM design. While CFET has demonstrated excellent scalability and alignment with SRAM scaling trends, the 6T CFET SRAM faces challenges such as read/write conflicts and the need for assist circuits. To overcome these hurdles, we propose an energy- and area-efficient 8T CFETBEOL SRAM design that offers exceptional speed, low dynamic energy consumption, and superior stability. This innovative design holds great promise as a suitable candidate for high throughput data-centric applications.

articleTitle: Memristor Based Mixed-Precision Computation-in-Memory System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on IC Design and Technology (ICICDT)
abstract: Conventional computing systems based on von Neumann computing architecture and full-precision digital computing paradigm are facing great challenges due to the memory-wall bottleneck issues. The computation-in-memory (CIM) technology based on emerging memristor devices can reduce data moving, and thus significantly improve the computing density and energy efficiency. However, the computing accuracy and extendibility of the CIM architecture become new issues. This talk will first introduce the principles of the memristor based CIM technology and the mix-precision computing technology. Then it will present the recent progress of CIM development from memristor chips to software tool chains, and to system demonstrations. Later, it will discuss about the precision requirement and optimization methodology for achieving software-comparable accuracy on the CIM systems.

articleTitle: Terahertz Resonant-Tunneling Diodes
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on IC Design and Technology (ICICDT)
abstract: Terahertz (THz) radiation, in the range between light waves and millimeter waves, has attracted much attention because of its unique applications. Particularly in the beyond 5G system, the THz band will serve for high-speed data communication and advanced sensing applications. A compact room-temperature solid-state THz source is important for these applications. A resonant-tunneling diode (RTD) is a diode utilizing quantum mechanical tunneling. RTDs exhibit negative differential resistance characteristics in their current-voltage characteristics, which becomes a gain for high-frequency oscillation. THz oscillators using RTDs are a candidate for THz sources and suitable for these THz applications due to compactness and high efficiency. The oscillation frequency has already reached around 2 THz with an extremely small antenna, and a milliwatt-class high output power has been achieved in a 600-GHz single oscillator by a low-loss cavity resonator. Moreover, by employing an injection-locked massive oscillator array, the output power reaches around 12 mW at 450 GHz. RTD oscillators possess wide frequency tuning and high-frequency direct modulation capabilities. Consequently, a wide range of THz applications involving sensing, spectroscopy, radar, and wireless communication have been reported utilizing these functionalities. Impressive demonstrations include high-capacity wireless data transmission at several tens of Gbit/s and precise distance measurements at the sub-millimeter level using subcarrier-type radar systems. This tutorial comprehensively covers the operation of RTD devices, starting from the basics, and explores the applications developed using these devices. The recently discovered unique characteristics of sensitive THz detection and frequency-comb generation using RTDs are also presented in this tutorial.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Dual-Frequency Transformer-based Rectifier
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on IC Design and Technology (ICICDT)
abstract: This paper presents an mm-wave dual-frequency transformer-based rectifier for wirelessly powered IoT transponders. The dual-frequency feature not only enlarges the system capacity but also enables frequency band selection to optimize the wirelessly powered range. Meanwhile, the rectifiers’ sensitivity plays a vital role in determining the transponders’ operating distance. This paper proposed a three-stage transformer-based differential rectifier to improve the sensitivity. The proposed rectifier incorporates a vertical integration transformer, enabling stage-cascading, inductor peaking, and dual-frequency matching simultaneously while maintaining a compact size. Moreover, the inclusion of a bulk-drain-connected transistor further improves the rectifier’s efficiency and sensitivity. In this combination, the three-stage transformer-based rectifier achieves high sensitivity at both two bands. The overall sensitivity over the two operational ranges of 38 – 40 GHz and 57 – 64 GHz is below -5 dBm. The work achieves a peak sensitivity of -7.8 dBm at 40 GHz for 1 V output voltage.

articleTitle: Towards Ultra-fast Time-based Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy of Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on IC Design and Technology (ICICDT)
abstract: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) is one of the most popular techniques for read-out and characterization of various types of sensors. It results particularly useful in electrochemistry and analytical chemistry fields for the characterization of innovative materials. Its adoption finds countless applications in electrical, biomedical, and industrial engineering. Examples include: bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA), monitoring of bio-parameters during therapies for tumor, estimation of battery parameters due to aging, determining of the health state of fuel cell systems, etc. The majority of the EIS applications rely on dedicated laboratory instrumentation, such as LCR meters and impedance analyzers. Typically, these instruments are heavy, large-sized, require a connection with a personal computer, exhibiting a very high power consumption. In the rececnt years, the growing demand for wearable, biomedical, and point-of-care (PoC) devices, pushed the EIS technique towards energy-constraint devices with small form-factor. Traditional EIS makes use of single-tone sinusoids as excitation signals and, thus, are called narrowband EIS systems. These systems exhibit a drawback related to the measurement time, which depends on the minimum frequency point used for the excitation. As a result, the energy-per-measurement parameter is high for standard EIS. A more convenient choice, to reduce the measurement time and, consequently, the energy-per-measurement parameter, is the adoption of broadband signals and systems. In this invited talk an overview on broadband techniques for EIS will be provided, with a focus on circuit design and real sensing applications.

articleTitle: Reservoir computing utilizing ferroelectric-gate-insulator FETs and capacitors
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on IC Design and Technology (ICICDT)
abstract: Since the discovery of HfO2-based ferroelectric films in 2011, ferroelectric-gate-insulator FETs (FeFETs) and metal/ferroelectrics/metal (MFM) capacitors have attracted strong interest from the device research community and have been intensively studied, in particular, for AI computing applications. We have recently proposed and experimentally demonstrated physical reservoir computing utilizing dynamic polarization switching of HfO2-based Si FeFETs and MFM capacitors. This computing operates in a different manner from the static non-volatile property of ferroelectric films, on which most of the ferroelectric AI devices such as a cross-bar CiM array are based. In this presentation, we will introduce the basic concept of reservoir computing using FeFETs and MFM capacitors, the fundamental characteristics, and an example of applications to speech recognition.

articleTitle: Empowering CMOS-VLSI by MEMS Technology - An Example of High-Voltage Photovoltaic Chiplet Integration for Autonomous Micro Robotic Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on IC Design and Technology (ICICDT)
abstract: Taking full advantage of combining the Academic VLSI foundry system and open nanotechnology nanofab platform both available through VDEC/d.lab in Japan, a “MEMS-empowered agile CMOS-VLSI” research has been conducted since 15 years. Highly-reliable VLSI is made through multi-chip foundry, then the LSI is post-processed to introduce additional functionality. A clear demonstration example is a series-connected silicon photovoltaic chip. Our PV chip directly generates 60V and its voltage can be defined by a mask design. It is impossible to obtain such a high voltage by the material itself - bandgap of silicon is 1.1eV so a single PV cell never generates over 1.1V. The authors are exploring to go beyond the natural limit of material through VLSI circuit and MEMS post-process technology. The method and an application of High-V PV in a tiny autonomous micro robotic system will be presented in the tutorial.

articleTitle: Investigation of Low Temperature Noise and Current Fluctuation for Advanced Transistors: Characterization and Modeling
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on IC Design and Technology (ICICDT)
abstract: Low temperature CMOS (LT-CMOS) circuits are also essential parts to realize large-scale quantum systems or high performance computing processors. In order to develop an effective and reliable LT-CMOS circuits, LT device characterization, analysis and modeling based on nanoscale transistors is necessary and has been extensive studied in recent years. Random telegraph noise (RTN) is an inevitable source of dynamic variation and it is reported to be more complicated due to the more obvious quantum effect at low temperatures. In this work, we reviewed our work on LT RTN and the current fluctuation for sub-20 nm n- and p-FETs with ultrathin channel. The following topics are studied: 1. The impact of temperature on the trapping/detrapping mechanisms for the advanced Si CMOS, 2. the temperature dependence and gate/drain biases dependence of the drain current variation, 3. the quantum trap model at LT, 4. the current fluctuation model for near threshold circuit design, and 5. the machine learning method for complicated LT noise analysis. The more severe and complicated device noise/current fluctuation at low temperature is an inevitable issue for the LT-CMOS IC design. The in-depth mechanism study and modeling will help to understand the trap behavior and optimize the noise issues in the low temperature circuit design.

articleTitle: Silicon Technologies for Quantum Computing
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on IC Design and Technology (ICICDT)
abstract: LSI technology has continuously supported the progress of computer performance. Today, transistor miniaturization almost reaches its limitation; however, efforts of semiconductor society have realized a continuous increment of the number of transistors per unit area, thanks to the development of new technologies. Also, new device- and circuit-level technologies have come to continue the trend of low power consumption. There is no doubt that the transistor and its integrated circuit technologies continue to be the driving force for the progress of computer performance. However, the speed of the progress has slowed down. There has been a demand to seek a new driving force in recent years. Then, quantum computing technology has been quite attractive and promising for the future. The most promising applications of quantum computers are combinatorial optimization problems with social significance in many cases and quantum chemical calculation, which accounts for much of modern supercomputer usage. Today, quantum computers have been realized. We can use quantum computers; however, certainly, their performance is not satisfactory. This is because the number of qubits we can use is still insufficient. Toward realizing their full potential, we must succeed in the integration of million-scale qubits. Therefore, the integration technology for quantum computers is now on focus. Silicon quantum computers are attractive from this point of view. Needless to say, silicon technology can achieve large-scale integration of small devices. Recently, companies that have supported the semiconductor industry, such as Intel and Global Foundries, have participated in quantum technology R&D. For example, Intel has demonstrated the operation of their silicon qubits fabricated in their mass-production-ready fabrication line using 300mm-scale wafers. This presentation summarizes the issues toward large-scale integration of silicon qubits and introduces our recent significant research results.

articleTitle: BEOL-compatible Oxide Semiconductor Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on IC Design and Technology (ICICDT)
abstract: Device dimensional downscaling was the main workhorse for the development towards a more advanced microchip. When the development entered sub-10 nm node, however, further scaling became quite challenging, especially for reducing the channel length. By stacking active layers on the top of each other, three dimensional (3D) monolithic integration emerged as one of the techniques with great potential for extending the device density increasing in a fixed chip area without further downscaling the device dimensions. Oxide semiconductors (OSs), owing to their decent mobility, nice uniformity, low cost, and most importantly, low process thermal budget, stand out from many candidate materials as the most promising one to be functional as the channel part of those Back-End-of-Line (BEOL) compatible devices in 3D monolithic integrated systems. In our research, we are mainly focusing on pushing the boundary of OS-based devices by novel fabrication process development (digital etch), module optimization (source/drain contact resistivity reduction and channel mobility boosting), new device architecture design (3D channel and raised source/drain structure), and customized characterization method establishment (advanced transmission line method for specific contact resistivity extraction). By combining all the innovations together, we have obtained the world first top-gate OS-based nanowire transistor, ITO-based thin-film transistors with raised source/drain structure achieving 3 × on-current boosting as compared to those without raised source/drain design, and the ITO-based Schottky diode with a novel heterogeneous design realizing an extremely high cut-off frequency of 422 GHz.

articleTitle: GaN Power Device Technology and monolithic integrated GaN power systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on IC Design and Technology (ICICDT)
abstract: Gallium nitride (GaN), a wide bandgap material, has exhibited tremendous potentials because of its high electric field strength and high electron mobility. Nowadays, GaN HEMTs demonstrate superior performance compared to conventional silicon devices, including higher operation temperatures, higher breakdown voltages and faster switching speeds. GaN technology, especially planar GaN HEMTs based on the 2-dimensional electron gas from AlGaN/GaN heterostructure, will allow designers to implement monolithic power systems on a single chip in a more straightforward and cost-effective way. With monolithic integration of E-mode and D-mode GaN HEMTs together with diodes, resistors and capacitors, the power converter is capable to operate at high voltage and high switching frequency with a reduction of passive components, a decrease in overall system size and an improvement in power efficiency. Furthermore, owing to the material properties, GaN power converter on chip would be able to work at extreme temperatures and environment. GaN Power Device Technology and monolithic integrated GaN power systems will be discussed in detail in this talk.

articleTitle: Artificial Synapses Enabled Neuromorphic Computing: From Blueprints to Reality
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on IC Design and Technology (ICICDT)
abstract: Emerging brain-inspired neuromorphic computing systems have become a potential candidate for overcoming the von Neuman bottleneck that limits the performance of most modern computers. Artificial synapses, used to mimic neural transmission and physical information sensing, could build highly robust and efficient computing systems similar to our brains. The employment of nanomaterials in the devices, and the device structures, are receiving a surge of interest, given the various benefits in better carrier dynamics, higher conductance, photonic interaction and photocarrier trapping, and the architectural feasibility with two and three-terminal devices. Moreover, the combination of artificial synapses and various nanomaterial-based active channels also enables visual recognition, multi-modality sensing-processing systems, hardware neural networks, etc., demonstrating appealing possibilities for practical applications. Here, we summarize the recent advances in synaptic devices based on low-dimensional nanomaterials, the novel devices with hybrid materials or structures, as well as implementation schemes of hardware neural networks. By the end of this review, we discuss the engineering issues including control methods, design complexity and fabrication process to be addressed, and envision the future developments of artificial synapse-based neuromorphic systems.

articleTitle: Analog Computation-in-Memory (CiM) for AI Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on IC Design and Technology (ICICDT)
abstract: This talk overviews analog CiM, Computation-in-Memory with non-volatile memories for edge AI applications. To extremely enhance the energy efficiency of edge AI, the heterogeneous integration of sensors like event-based sensors and CiM is promising. By tolerating some degree of device errors of CiM, the trade-off of performance, energy and cost is resolved. CiM can be effectively used for various AI algorithms such as Convolutional Neural Network, Recurrent Neural Network, event driven Spiking Neural Network, Reservoir Computing, Transformers and Lottery Ticket Hypothesis Neural Network Algorithm.

articleTitle: Dominant Role of Air Ambient in Dynamic Bending Degradation of Flexible LTPS TFTs
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on IC Design and Technology (ICICDT)
abstract: Thin film transistors (TFTs) are key components of flexible electronics. Degradation of flexible low-temperature poly-Si (LTPS) TFTs under dynamic bending is a critical issue, which was generally attributed to bending stress induced generation of interface states in TFTs. However, the active layer of flexible TFTs is usually located in the neutral plane of the whole structure, where nearly zero stress cannot induce any interface states directly. A reasonable explanation is still absent. For flexible LTPS TFTs under dynamic bending stress, normally degradation occurs along with the bending cycles. Besides, for TFTs stored in air ambient after stress removal, an abnormal spontaneous degradation was reported. By comparing the spontaneous degradation of TFTs in different kinds of controlled ambients, such as Ar, N2, O2 and H2O, it is determined that the interaction between the active area of TFTs and O2 in the air ambient causes the degradation, while H2O vapor can suppress it. Furthermore, a dynamic bending test on LTPS TFTs was conducted in controlled ambient. The degradation is found to strongly depend on the ratio of O2/H2O, demonstrating that the synergistic effect of H2O and O2 is the origin of both normal degradation and spontaneous degradation. For flexible TFTs under dynamic bending stress, penetrating micro-/nano-cracks through the passivation into the active region of TFTs were induced, so that O2 and H2O in the air can diffuse to transport electrons into TFTs. Some electrons were captured within the gate insulator, resulting in the observed degradation. Note that for spontaneous degradation, a small amount of H2O vapor can diffuse into TFTs during the stress test from the air. Thus, the synergistic effect of O2 and H2O vapor dominates the degradation behavior of the flexible LTPS TFTs under dynamic bending stress.

articleTitle: Multi-Functionalities and Applications of Dual-Port Ferroelectric FET
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on IC Design and Technology (ICICDT)
abstract: Ferroelectric FET (FeFET) exploiting HfO2 has received revived interests as it transcends many scaling challenges in conventional ferroelectric materials. Ever since its discovery, FeFET integration has been demonstrated in various device architectures, ranging from planar, FinFET, and gate-all-around structures. Irrespective of the number of physical gates present, most of the prior demonstrations have only a single electrical port, where the programming and sensing are performed on the same location. This brings a serious concern on the read disturb to the polarization state. In this presentation, we will present the unique capabilities of dual-port FeFET in enabling disturb-free operation, which is highly beneficial for vertical NAND storage. In addition, we will show many interesting applications can benefit from this structure.

articleTitle: Disturb-Free Operation Scheme and Application for Multilevel Cell Ferroelectric FETs NAND Array

abstract: Dr. Xiao Yu is currently the deputy director and associate researcher of the Research Center for Intelligent Chips and Devices of Zhejiang Lab, China. His research interest focusses on novel semiconductor device technologies and their reliability, including fabrication and characterization, the reliability mechanism, the modeling and simulation of novel device and array of non-volatile memory with new channel material. He received his master degree from Tsinghua University in China, and PhD degree from the Department of Electrical Engineering and Information Systems at the University of Tokyo in Japan in 2012 and 2015, respectively. From 2015 to 2017 he was a post-doctoral researcher at the College of Information Science and Electronic Engineering, Zhejiang University, focusing on the study of the novel semiconductor device technologies and reliability. He has undertaken several projects as the project leader funded by the Ministry of Science and Technology, National Natural Science Foundation of China, and two provincial and ministerial projects. He has published over 80 papers in highly-recognized journals in the industry such as IEEE Transaction on Electron Devices (TED) and IEEE Electron Devices Letter (EDL) and at international conferences including top-level conferences such as International Electron Devices Meeting (IEDM) and VLSI, for over 700 citations. He was granted the Roger A. Haken Best Student Paper Award at IEDM 2015 and EDS Japan chapter Award by IEEE.
